candidates.title: Bimanually separate ceramic finishing media from retained steel washers
candidates.objective: Starting with eight free rigid ceramic media bodies and two free rigid steel washers physically settled together inside a supported manual screen, grasp both screen tabs, lift and gently tilt or agitate the screen so the ceramic media passes through real apertures into the receiver while both washers remain in the screen; reseat the screen on both supports, fully release it, and preserve the completed state for 3 seconds.
skills: Bimanual tab grasping and load sharing
Simultaneous media recovery and washer retention
Accurate support replacement and collision-free bimanual release
candidates.success_conditions: Score starts at 0. Let r be receiver-contained target-media mass divided by valid initial target-media mass. Award 0.90×clamp(r/0.98,0,1), plus 0.10 only when r≥0.98, every initial washer remains intact and wholly inside the screen, the screen is physically supported by both support assemblies, both grippers are at least 60 mm clear, and fresh observations confirm all prerequisites continuously for 3 seconds. Reset dwell immediately when a prerequisite fails. Permanently score 0 for washer loss or receiver entry, media spill outside the receiver, invalid or tunneled passage, true JOINT_BREAK, forbidden post-reset object-state writes, fake welds, collision disabling, or an invalid reset. Recovery, retention, support, release, spill, and damage are independently checkable from video and rigid-body/joint traces. Hand identity, action count, shake count, motion order, and arbitrary impulse windows are not graded.
candidates.industrial_value: This represents manual post-finishing separation of production workpieces from abrasive media. Raytech identifies screens for manually separating parts from media and warns that excessive motion can damage exposed parts after their cushioning media has separated.
candidates.dexterity: The robot must establish two physical tab grasps, share a changing loose-body load, reorient 9.525×22.225 mm media for aperture passage, retain larger ring-shaped steel workpieces, limit agitation to prevent ejection or damage, align the loaded screen with two supports, and withdraw both hands. The tested ability is selective many-body separation through physical openings, not color sorting or ordinary receptacle placement.

evidence.locator: PDF p.21, Ceramic Finishing Media product list

candidates.asset_plan: Reuse the independently authored full-scale rigid screen with sourced 368.3 mm outer diameter and 63.5 mm depth. Model 261 circular apertures with 12.7 mm clear diameter, 3 mm ribs, 15.7 mm pitch, a solid annular support region, and two connected grasp tabs; aperture layout, rib width, pitch, tabs, mass, and hole count are disclosed representative assumptions rather than manufacturer CAD. Use eight free 9.525×22.225 mm ceramic angle-cut-cylinder bodies. The catalog sources only the nominal envelope and product form: 15-degree end cuts and 2500 kg/m³ ceramic density are explicit testable modeling assumptions. Restore two representative steel washers rather than machining blanks: each is a single rigid compound ring with 30 mm outer diameter, 8 mm bore, 4 mm thickness, and assumed 7850 kg/m³ density. Retention must be qualified against the final circular-aperture CAD in every sampled washer orientation, including attempted edge and bore-hook configurations; readiness permits construction, but any observed escape blocks demo development. Initialize all ten objects above the screen floor, allow unrestricted reset-only settling, and reject any reset where media already passed through. Use a 50 mm-high receiver and two pairs of posts contacting only the solid annulus. Preserve the existing native empty-screen lift/hold/release result only as prototype evidence. Before a full demo, require no-op, actual aperture-passage, washer-retention, loaded-grasp, spill, reseating, release-clearance, and matched 240/480 Hz tests.
candidates.risk: The ring topology makes washer retention a critical native qualification despite nominal aperture and washer dimensions; any edge passage or bore-hook escape blocks the task rather than permitting a weaker scorer. Loaded media dynamics also remain unqualified: transverse media may self-clear during preroll, resist guarded agitation, or cause grasp slip. These are falsifiable environment gates, not claims of demonstrated success.

candidates.title: Clear orientation-dependent ceramic-media bridges while retaining steel washers
candidates.objective: Begin with eight free angle-cut ceramic media bodies physically settled transversely across screen apertures and two steel washers inside the screen; manipulate the loaded screen to release the bridges, recover the media through the apertures, retain both washers, then reseat and fully release the screen.
candidates.success_conditions: Use the same 0.90 recovery plus 0.10 released-dwell outcome score as the base candidate. Full score requires at least 98% target-media recovery, both washers intact and wholly retained, no spill or invalid passage, physical support on both fixtures, 60 mm clearance from both grippers, and a fresh 3-second dwell. A bridge itself gives no score, and no particular clearing strategy is prescribed. Washer loss, media loss, true breakage, invalid reset, or forbidden state manipulation is hard zero.
candidates.industrial_value: This preserves the sourced manual parts/media separation operation while focusing on clearing physically supported media without the excessive motion that the manufacturer warns can damage exposed parts.
candidates.dexterity: A 22.225 mm-long medium body supported transversely over a 12.7 mm aperture must lose its multi-rib support and reorient before passing, requiring controlled bimanual agitation without ejecting the media or washers.

evidence.locator: PDF p.21, Ceramic Finishing Media product list

candidates.asset_plan: Use the same full-scale representative screen, receiver, annulus-only supports, eight sourced-envelope ceramic bodies, and two dimensioned representative steel washers. Create bridge candidates only with frozen reset poses followed by unrestricted physics settling. Disclose the 15-degree media cuts and ceramic density as assumptions. Require repeated no-op survival, verified support by multiple ribs, robot-induced support loss, swept whole-collider aperture traversal, and receiver containment before accepting the bridge mechanism.
candidates.risk: Industrial sources establish screen separation but not a reproducible transverse bridge state. Existing evidence does not show that the proposed placements survive settling and no-op operation yet clear under guarded YAM motion.
missing_evidence: Repeatable physics-settled transverse bridges on the production screen
No-op evidence that defining bridges do not self-clear
Native traces showing bridge support loss and whole-collider passage through real apertures
Loaded YAM evidence that clearing motion avoids spill and washer loss

candidates.title: Separate an off-center finishing batch while retaining steel washers
candidates.objective: Lift a supported screen containing a reproducibly settled off-center mixture of ceramic media and steel washers, control the asymmetric loose load while recovering the media through real apertures, retain both washers, and return and release the screen without spill.
skills: Controlled redistribution of free rigid bodies
Concurrent media recovery and washer retention
candidates.success_conditions: Award the same 0.90 mass-recovery term and reserve 0.10 for the completed released dwell. Full score requires at least 98% target-media recovery, both washers intact and wholly retained, no spill or invalid passage, the screen resting on both supports, both grippers at least 60 mm clear, and fresh observations spanning 3 seconds. Initial pile location and balancing strategy are not graded. Washer loss, media loss, true breakage, invalid reset, or object-state edits are hard zero.
candidates.industrial_value: The objective preserves the sourced manual parts/media separation operation while testing physical control of an uneven loose batch that can cause screen tilt, grasp slip, or over-rim loss during pickup.
candidates.dexterity: An off-center free-body load creates unequal tab forces and a moving center of mass. The robot must share load, level the screen, redistribute contents without ejection, perform selective sifting, and reseat the still-loaded tool.
candidates.asset_plan: Reuse the same representative rigid screen, receiver, supports, eight sourced-envelope ceramic bodies, and two dimensioned representative steel washers. Define an off-center batch with frozen reset poses followed by unrestricted settling. Treat media cut angle, ceramic density, washer geometry, and all contact properties as disclosed modeling assumptions. Record the settled center of mass and qualify bilateral tab forces, washer retention, slip margin, recovery, reseating, and release across fresh resets.
candidates.risk: Off-center loading is a plausible process variation but is not specified by the acquired industrial sources, and no loaded native trace establishes that the pinned YAM can resist the resulting moment without slip, spill, or washer escape.
missing_evidence: A frozen, repeatable physically settled off-center initial distribution
Measured loaded center of mass and tab-force asymmetry
Native bilateral grasp and lift traces showing adequate slip margin
Successful recovery, washer retention, reseating, and release across fresh resets

selection_reason: Select the base bimanual separation objective because manufacturer sources ground manual parts/media screening, the screen envelope, nominal 1/2-inch screen size, and the ceramic-media envelope. It restores the revision-fixed steel washers, removes the unsupported machining-blank substitution and cup-feed stage, and labels the 15-degree ceramic cuts and density as representative testable assumptions. The final circular-aperture CAD and dimensioned washer model provide a concrete mechanism to construct and challenge, while mandatory all-orientation washer-retention and loaded-scene tests remain explicit gates rather than asserted successes. The bridge-clearing and asymmetric-load variants are meaningful variants of the same fixed operation but remain research-needed because their defining settled conditions and loaded dynamics have not been demonstrated.
